title: Does an Executable Generate–Validate–Repair Loop Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated NetOps Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline (guarded) reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow (baseline). Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 tasks per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) we produced a single shared initial candidate per task via gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated the same candidate under both conditions. A deterministic emulator validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) enforced structured workflow policies and could trigger at most one repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline success = 120/120; guarded success = 120/120; contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces show repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes. We revise the manuscript by (1) condensing provenance into a compact instrumentation paragraph that points to archived execution and analysis artifacts, (2) adding a short formal binary scoring rule (pass/fail) with a concrete example taken from archived scorer/validator output, and (3) adding a concise nearest-work comparison matrix that marks where this study differs from the closest prior experiments. We retain the preregistered analysis and interpret the degenerate ceiling outcome, give design recommendations for follow-ups, and discuss construct/external validity limits.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) promise to translate operator intent into concrete network configuration commands, potentially improving NetOps productivity. However, syntactically plausible commands can violate workflow invariants (for example, changing MTU without an enforced shutdown or performing hazardous uplink switchover), causing semantic failures only visible in closed-loop execution. Prior work therefore recommends integrating verification, emulation, digital twins, or veto layers so generated candidates are validated before enactment. Evaluating guarded pipelines requires executable tests that detect semantic and stateful failures beyond token- or syntax-level correctness.

We executed a preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) designed to isolate the marginal effect of an executable validator and a bounded repair policy on identical generator outputs. The central confirmatory research question was: Does integrating an executable network emulator as a validator in a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce semantic/network-level failures when enacting LLM-generated configuration changes compared to an LLM-only suggestion workflow? To isolate validator/repair effects we used a shared-initial-candidate paired design: each task produced one generator output that was scored both as baseline (LLM-only) and as guarded (validator±repair). This design removes generator-induced variability across paired episodes and directly measures validator/repair influence on identical candidates.

Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered, artifact-rich paired experiment (N=120) that holds the generator fixed and measures the incremental effect of an executable validator plus bounded repair; (2) complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation demonstrating completion of the preregistered protocol; (3) an artifact-grounded analysis and interpretation of a degenerate ceiling outcome (100% success in both conditions) including exact McNemar and bootstrap reporting; and (4) concrete methodological recommendations for future confirmatory designs that will exercise repair behavior.
sections.related_work:
We position this study relative to two primary lines of recent work. First, executable emulation and closed-loop benchmarks emphasize that text- or syntax-level correctness does not guarantee safe enactment; closed-loop emulators expose sequencing and stateful errors (make-before-break mistakes, group-availability violations) that token checks miss. Representative works that build executable NetOps test harnesses include NetConfArena and other closed-loop benchmark efforts. Second, a growing literature proposes tool-augmented agent architectures and bounded-autonomy guardrails (veto layers, translation-to-formal-model, generate→validate→repair) to improve operational safety. Surveys and prototype tool papers document architectural patterns and prototype gains but often conflate generator variability with verification efficacy.

Nearest-work comparison (compact matrix). The following concise matrix lists closest prior empirical or benchmark studies and marks how this study differs (columns: shared-generation paired design; executable emulator validator; repair budget ≤1; synthetic deterministic task corpus; single hosted model tested):
- Benchmarking LLM-Driven Network Configuration Repair (arXiv:2604.22513): focuses on generator/repair pipelines in benchmarks; differs: most prior evaluations generate independently per condition (not shared paired), and some perform multi-model comparisons; our study isolates validator marginal effect via shared-generation.
- NetConfArena (arXiv:2608.23179): executable closed-loop benchmark; differs: NetConfArena evaluates model–harness interactions broadly; our work uses a paired shared-candidate design to measure validator/repair marginal effect on identical outputs.
- MeshAgent (conference paper, DOI:10.1145/3771567): presents a tool for reliable network management with LLMs; differs: primarily architecture/prototype focus rather than preregistered paired statistical testing isolating validator effect.
- Lightyear (BGP verification tooling, DOI:10.1145/3603269.3604842): verification-scaling work for specific control-plane properties; differs: formal verification emphasis (control-plane reachability) rather than a generate→validate→repair experimental protocol.
- Aether (arXiv:2604.18233): agentic AI + digital twin validation; differs: architectural/digital-twin approach and broader agentic workflows; our experiment fixes generator outputs to measure validator marginality.

This compressed comparison shows that (a) executable emulation is necessary to observe stateful semantic failures, and (b) a shared-generation paired design is a different experimental lens that isolates validator/repair marginal effects from generator variance.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan. The study was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) before execution. The preregistration specified a paired-binary confirmatory design with N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks partitioned deterministically into three topology classes (edge/core/leaf–spine) with 40 tasks each. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the prespecified test was the exact two-sided McNemar. A bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was included for the paired-difference estimate. The preregistration also defined exclusion/contamination rules, a repair budget (≤1 repair per guarded episode), deterministic reset controls, and sensitivity analyses.

Task generation, shared-generation design, and validator semantics. Tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each task manifest contains initial_state, expected_final_state, natural-language intent, required_sequence (canonical ordered operations), and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, difficulty level). For each task we performed a single shared initial candidate generation using the declared model (gpt-5-mini). The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version=5.0), an executable emulator/validator that applies task-encoded workflow policies (for example: must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, make-before-break). The validator executes the candidate in an emulated state checker and emits a structured validator_trace containing validation_before, validation_after, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, and repair_applied. The preregistered repair policy invoked at most one repair iteration when validator.violation_count>0; repair prompts and provider traces were archived when generated.

Compact instrumentation and artifact pointers. To avoid provenance clutter in the main text we summarize key archived artifacts and point readers to the packaged execution and analysis archive (full manifest and detailed JSONL artifacts are archived): core execution artifacts include execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/responses/, and execution/provider_calls/. Primary analysis artifacts include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, and analysis/missingness_summary.csv. Representative scoring/validator outputs for inspected examples are present under execution/scoring/*.json. The archived bundle contains exhaustive checksums and the preregistration manifest; readers can use those archives to reproduce exact reconciliation steps.

Formal binary scoring rule (explicit). The preregistered paired binary outcome (pass = 1, fail = 0) used to populate the McNemar table is defined by this deterministic decision logic, applied to each episode's scoring/validator artifact:
1) If scorer.score == 1 and validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true and validator_trace.validation_after.violation_count == 0, then outcome = pass (1).
2) Else if scorer.score == 0 or validator_trace.validation_after.valid == false or validator_trace.validation_after.violation_count > 0, then outcome = fail (0).
3) If an episode lacks either a completed scorer or a completed validator_trace (technical/instrumentation failure), the episode is marked as a technical exclusion per the preregistration and archived; excluded pairs are reported in missingness summaries. No such exclusions occurred in this run.

Concrete example from archived artifact. Execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (archived) illustrates a pass under the above rule: the artifact records score = 1; validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true; validator_trace.validation_after.violation_count = 0; normalized_response equals the expected normalized_reference_answer. Under the scoring rule this episode is labeled pass = 1 and contributes to n_11 in the paired contingency table.
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary outcome. The run completed without technical exclusions: planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120 (one shared generation per pair). Condition-level summaries record baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0, guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0 (success rates = 1.0 for both). The paired contingency table records n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Validator traces report repair_applied = false for all guarded episodes.

Per-topology outcomes. The preregistered deterministic partition produced 40 tasks per topology class. Per-topology results are:
- Edge (40 tasks): baseline 40/40 success; guarded 40/40 success.
- Core (40 tasks): baseline 40/40 success; guarded 40/40 success.
- Leaf–spine (40 tasks): baseline 40/40 success; guarded 40/40 success.
These counts are available in the archived representative scoring artifacts and in analysis/condition_summary.csv (referenced above).

Representative diagnostic. Representative scoring artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json) show normalized_response equals normalized_reference_answer; parsed_command_count equals required_command_count from the task payload; validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true; validator_trace.repair_applied = false. Because validator.violation_count = 0 for every guarded episode, the preregistered repair budget was unused and no repair_provider_trace artifacts were generated.

Contamination, missingness, and reconciliation. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty and analysis/missingness_summary.csv reports complete_pairs = 120 with zero technical/instrumentation exclusions. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact confirms provider-call audits and pair accounting are internally consistent. These reconciliations support the integrity of the confirmatory statistics reported above.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting the ceiling outcome. The shared-generation paired design isolates validator/repair marginal effects by removing generator variance, but it also produces a risk: if the generator and prompt strategy produce valid candidates for the chosen task bank, the guarded path has nothing to repair. That is precisely what occurred: all 120 shared initial candidates satisfied the deterministic validator and no repairs were applied, producing n_11 = 120 and a degenerate paired-difference estimate of 0.00 with CI [0.00, 0.00]. The exact McNemar p = 1.0 reflects complete concordance; the bootstrap CI degeneracy is an expected consequence of zero discordant pairs under the preregistered resampling scheme.

Design trade-offs and recommendations for future confirmatory studies. Based on archived difficulty metadata and the observed absence of repairs, we recommend the following preregistered adjustments when the research aim is to detect repair utility:
1) Independent per-condition generation: permit separate draws per condition so guarded pipelines can intercept generator variance that produces invalid candidates; pair using blocking or covariate adjustment to retain partial control.
2) Targeted task selection: concentrate confirmatory power on tasks labeled 'very_hard' or with high dependency_rule_count to increase generator-induced violations.
3) Prespecified prompt perturbations: apply controlled prompt perturbations on a deterministic subset to raise generator error incidence while preserving other paired blocks.
4) Flexible repair budgets for exploratory arms: allow multiple repair iterations to evaluate repair convergence and cost.

Operational and audit implications. Even when unused, a deterministic validator that emits structured traces (checked rules, touched fields, why repair was not applied) supports operator auditability and post-hoc analysis. The archived artifacts demonstrate end-to-end instrumented accounting (provider-call audits, scoring traces, deterministic reconciliation) that can be repurposed for operator-facing explanations and third-party audits. The experiment also underscores that claims about repair benefits require careful experimental framing: an idle guard does not imply absence of need in other generator/prompt/task combinations.

Threats to validity (concise). Internal validity: strong due to deterministic resets, exhaustive audit logs, and no exclusions. Construct validity: limited by policy encodings derived from synthetic task payloads; the validator enforces canonical constraints but does not emulate all vendor-specific behaviors. External validity: constrained by the synthetic deterministic task corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Conclusion validity: preregistered power assumptions (baseline failure ≈0.40) were violated (observed baseline = 0.00), rendering the confirmatory test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness with a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini). All 120 shared initial candidates passed the deterministic emulator validator, yielding n_11 = 120 and a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The result documents a ceiling for this curated synthetic task bank and demonstrates that a shared-generation paired design can mask repair benefits that would appear if generators sometimes produce invalid candidates. Our principal scientific contribution is methodological: we show how a preregistered, artifact-rich paired design cleanly isolates validator/repair effects and how deterministic archival artifacts (task manifests, validator traces, provider-call audits, and reconciliation files) enable reproducible failure analysis and transparent auditing even when the primary confirmatory test is degenerate. The archived artifacts permit follow-up studies that relax the shared-generation constraint, compare generator families, expand repair budgets, and evaluate more production-rooted corpora to quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
